(sec-module-robotics.motion)=
# Module: robotics.motion

functionality for motion including generation of trajectories with acceleration profiles,
path planning and motion

- **Author**: Johannes Gerstmayr
- **Date**: 2022-02-16

(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profileconstantacceleration)=
## CLASS ProfileConstantAcceleration (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: class to create a constant acceleration (optimal) PTP trajectory; trajectory ignores global max. velocities and accelerations

- **input**:
  - `finalCoordinates`: list or numpy array with final coordinates for profile
  - `duration`: duration (time) for profile
- **output**: returns profile object, which is then used to compute interpolated trajectory

(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilelinearaccelerationslist)=
## CLASS ProfileLinearAccelerationsList (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: class to create a linear acceleration PTP profile, using a list of accelerations to define the profile; the (joint) coordinates and velocities are computed relative to values of previous profiles; ignores global max. accelerations and velocities of Trajectory

- **input**:
  - `accelerationList`: list of tuples (relativeTime, accelerationVector) in which relativeTime is the time relative to the start of the profile (first time must be zero!) and accelerationVector is the list of accelerations of this time point, which is then linearly interpolated
- **output**: returns profile object, which is then used to compute interpolated trajectory in class Trajectory

*example*:

```python
  profile = ProfileLinearAccelerationsList([(0,[0.,1.,2]), (0,[1.,1.,-2])])
```

(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profileptp)=
## CLASS ProfilePTP (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: class to create a synchronous motion PTP trajectory, using max. accelerations and max velocities; duration automatically computed

- **input**:
  - `finalCoordinates`: list or numpy array with final coordinates for profile
  - `syncAccTimes`: True: all coordinates accelerate and decelerate at the same times, the motion is a straight line in the coordinates; False: each coordinate uses its largest acceleration, so that the motion deviates from this line (#3390)
  - `maxVelocities`: list or numpy array with maximum velocities; may be empty list []; used if smaller than globalMaxVelocities
  - `maxAccelerations`: list or numpy array with maximum accelerations; may be empty list []; used if smaller than globalMaxAccelerations
- **output**: returns profile object, which is then used to compute interpolated trajectory

- **class function description**: initialize ProfilePTP with final coordinates of motion, optionally max. velocities and accelerations just for this profile (overrides global settings)

(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilepolynomial5)=
## CLASS ProfilePolynomial5 (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: a point-to-point profile in which each coordinate follows the polynomial of degree 5 from rest to rest, with zero velocity and acceleration at both ends (#3262): s(t) = s0 + (s1 - s0) (10 tau^3 - 15 tau^4 + 6 tau^5), tau = (t - t0)/duration; the maximum velocity is 1.875 and the maximum acceleration 5.77 times (s1 - s0)/duration and (s1 - s0)/duration^2; the global maximum velocities and accelerations of Trajectory are not used

- **input**:
  - `finalCoordinates`: list or numpy array with the coordinates at the end of the profile
  - `duration`: the time of the profile

- **class function description**: the profile in Trajectory

(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilecartesianlinear(-profilecartesian))=
## CLASS ProfileCartesianLinear(_ProfileCartesian) (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: a Cartesian profile of a robot: the tool frame moves on a straight line from its frame at the start of the profile to finalHT, with its rotation about one fixed axis (exu.HT.InterpolateSO3), by the time law timeLaw (#3262); the joint coordinates by the analytic inverse kinematics of the robot (KinematicChain.InverseKinematicsAnalytic) at each evaluation, the solution nearest to the last one evaluated, the joint velocities from the twist of the tool by the Jacobian, the accelerations by their difference in time; a ValueError if a pose of the path is out of reach. It needs a robot of the analytic inverse kinematics (6 revolute joints with a spherical wrist or of the UR geometry); a path close to a singular configuration gives large joint velocities, a jump of the joint coordinates on the path (more than 0.5 rad in 1/200 of it) raises a ValueError

- **input**:
  - `robot`: the exudyn.robotics.Robot
  - `finalHT`: the tool frame at the end, exu.HT in global coordinates
  - `duration`: the time of the profile
  - `timeLaw`: 'polynomial5' (default) or 'constantAcceleration', the path parameter in time
  - `keepConfiguration`: True: the solutions in the arm configuration of the start (KinematicChain.ArmConfiguration), as a robot controller keeps it on a Cartesian path; a path on which it cannot be kept without a jump of the joint coordinates, through or close to a singular configuration, raises a ValueError; False: the solution nearest to the last one, which may change the configuration (#3272)

Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/staubliTX2blending.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/staubliTX2blending.py) (Ex), [`robotics/staubliTX2trajectories.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/staubliTX2trajectories.py) (Ex), [`robotCartesianPathsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCartesianPathsTest.py) (TM), [`robotTrajectoryProfilesTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotTrajectoryProfilesTest.py) (TM), [`trajectoryBlendingCartesianTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/trajectoryBlendingCartesianTest.py) (TM), [`trajectoryBlendingTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/trajectoryBlendingTest.py) (TM)


(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilecartesiancircular(-profilecartesian))=
## CLASS ProfileCartesianCircular(_ProfileCartesian) (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: a Cartesian profile of a robot (#3272): the tool position moves on the arc of the circle from its position at the start of the profile through viaPosition to the position of finalHT, the rotation of the tool from the start to that of finalHT about one fixed axis (exu.HT.InterpolateSO3), both by the time law timeLaw; the joint coordinates as in ProfileCartesianLinear; for a tool that turns with the arc, see ProfileCartesianScrew

- **input**:
  - `robot`: the exudyn.robotics.Robot
  - `viaPosition`: a point of the arc between the start and the end, in global coordinates
  - `finalHT`: the tool frame at the end, exu.HT in global coordinates
  - `duration`: the time of the profile
  - `timeLaw`: 'polynomial5' (default) or 'constantAcceleration', the path parameter in time
  - `keepConfiguration`: True: the arm configuration of the start is kept, see ProfileCartesianLinear

Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotCartesianPathsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCartesianPathsTest.py) (TM)


(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilecartesianscrew(-profilecartesian))=
## CLASS ProfileCartesianScrew(_ProfileCartesian) (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: a Cartesian profile of a robot (#3272): the tool frame moves as a rigid body by a screw motion from its frame at the start of the profile, the rotation by angle about the axis through axisPoint along axis together with the translation translation along it, both by the time law timeLaw; translation = 0 is the circle about the axis with the tool turning with it, angle = 0 the straight line along the axis; the joint coordinates as in ProfileCartesianLinear

- **input**:
  - `robot`: the exudyn.robotics.Robot
  - `axisPoint`: a point of the screw axis, in global coordinates
  - `axis`: the direction of the screw axis, in global coordinates (normalized)
  - `angle`: the angle of the rotation about the axis, in rad, positive by the right-hand rule
  - `translation`: the translation along the axis
  - `duration`: the time of the profile
  - `timeLaw`: 'polynomial5' (default) or 'constantAcceleration', the path parameter in time
  - `keepConfiguration`: True: the arm configuration of the start is kept, see ProfileCartesianLinear

Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotCartesianPathsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCartesianPathsTest.py) (TM)


(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-profilecartesianspline(-profilecartesian))=
## CLASS ProfileCartesianSpline(_ProfileCartesian) (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: a Cartesian profile of a robot (#3272): the tool position moves on the natural cubic spline through its position at the start of the profile and the positions of viaHTs, parametrized by the length of the chords between them; the rotation of the tool by the natural cubic spline of the rotation vectors of the frames relative to the start, on the same parameter (the rotations less than pi from the start), so that the position and the angular velocity are continuous at the via frames; the path parameter by the time law timeLaw; the last frame of viaHTs is the end; the joint coordinates as in ProfileCartesianLinear

- **input**:
  - `robot`: the exudyn.robotics.Robot
  - `viaHTs`: a list of the tool frames the path passes, exu.HT in global coordinates; the last is the end
  - `duration`: the time of the profile
  - `timeLaw`: 'polynomial5' (default) or 'constantAcceleration', the path parameter in time
  - `keepConfiguration`: True: the arm configuration of the start is kept, see ProfileCartesianLinear

Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotCartesianPathsTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotCartesianPathsTest.py) (TM)


(sec-module-robotics.motion-class-trajectory)=
## CLASS Trajectory (in module robotics.motion)

**class description**: class to define (PTP) trajectories for robots and multibody systems; trajectories are defined for a set of coordinates (e.g. joint angles or other coordinates which need to be interpolated over time)


*example*:

```python
  #create simple trajectory for two joint coordinates:
  traj = Trajectory(initialCoordinates=[1,1], initialTime=1)
  #add optimal trajectory with max. accelerations:
  traj.Add(ProfileConstantAcceleration([2.,3.],2.))
  traj.Add(ProfileConstantAcceleration([3.,-1.],2.))
  #add profile with limited velocities and accelerations:
  traj.Add(ProfilePTP([1,1],syncAccTimes=False, maxVelocities=[1,1], maxAccelerations=[5,5]))
  #now evaluate trajectory at certain time point (this could be now applied in a user function)
  [s,v,a] = traj.Evaluate(t=0.5)
```


(sec-motion-trajectory---init--)=
### Class function: __init__

[`__init__(self, initialCoordinates, initialTime = 0, maxVelocities = [], maxAccelerations = [], jumpTolerance = 1e-6)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/motion.py#L655)

- **class function description**: initialize robot link with parameters, being self-explaining
- **input**:
  - `initialTime`: initial time for initial coordinates
  - `initialCoordinates`: initial coordinates for profile
  - `maxVelocities`: list or numpy array to describe global maximum velocities per coordinate
  - `maxAccelerations`: list or numpy array to describe global maximum accelerations per coordinate
  - `jumpTolerance`: Add raises a ValueError if a profile starts at coordinates that differ by more than this from the end of the profile before, e.g. a Cartesian profile whose inverse kinematics starts in another solution (#3272)


(sec-motion-trajectory-fromwaypoints)=
### Class function: FromWaypoints

[`FromWaypoints(cls, waypoints, maxVelocities, maxAccelerations, blend = 'auto', blendFactor = 1., initialTime = 0.)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/motion.py#L682)

- **class function description**: A trajectory of point-to-point motions (ProfilePTP) through waypoints, blended so that the robot does not stop at each of them (#3383).
- **input**:
  - `waypoints`: the coordinates of the waypoints, one per row, at least two different ones; repeated waypoints are left out
  - `maxVelocities`: the largest velocity per coordinate
  - `maxAccelerations`: the largest acceleration per coordinate
  - `blend`: blendTimeWithNext for all profiles, 'auto' or a time; see Add
  - `blendFactor`: the blend times are multiplied by this factor; 0 stops at each waypoint
  - `initialTime`: the time at the start
- **output**: the Trajectory

(sec-motion-trajectory-add)=
### Class function: Add

[`Add(self, profile, blendTimeWithNext = 0., blendSpace = 'joint')`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/motion.py#L720)

- **class function description**: add successively profiles, using MotionProfile class; raises a ValueError if the profile starts at other coordinates than the trajectory ends, by more than jumpTolerance
- **input**:
  - `profile`: the profile, e.g. ProfilePTP, ProfilePolynomial5 or ProfileCartesianLinear
  - `blendTimeWithNext`: the time by which the next profile starts before this one ends (#3274): in this time, the trajectory is the sum of the motions of both (the superposition of the two rest-to-rest profiles), so that it passes near the end of this profile without stopping and reaches the end of the next one exactly; at most the duration of this profile and of the next; e.g. the deceleration time of this profile, if the next one accelerates in the same time, keeps the velocity of an axis that moves on in the same direction; without a next profile it has no effect; see GetBlendings and Evaluate(t, enableBlending). 'auto': when the next profile is added, the largest overlap - at most the deceleration phase of this profile and the acceleration phase of the next (half their durations for the profiles without phases) - in which the blended velocities stay within the limits: the peak velocities of the two profiles, so that the blending is not faster than they are, or maxVelocities of Trajectory where they are larger (#3283). With maxVelocities of Trajectory, a given blend time whose velocities exceed these limits raises a ValueError
  - `blendSpace`: 'joint': the motions of the joints are summed; 'cartesian': this profile and the next are Cartesian profiles (ProfileCartesianLinear, ...) of the same robot, and in the overlap the motions of the tool - its position and rotation from the start of the next profile - are summed, the joint coordinates follow by the inverse kinematics in the arm configuration of this profile; the tool then rounds the corner in the plane of two lines, while the blending of the joints lets it leave the paths (#3283)

- **class function description**: return interpolation of trajectory for coordinates, velocities and accelerations at given time

(sec-motion-trajectory-getblendings)=
### Class function: GetBlendings

[`GetBlendings(self, kinematicChain = None, numberOfSamples = 101)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/motion.py#L977)

- **class function description**: the blendings of the trajectory (#3274), one dict per profile with a blendTimeWithNext and a next profile: 'profile', its index; 'startTime' and 'endTime', the time in which the two profiles overlap; 'viaCoordinates', the end of the profile, which the blended trajectory passes near; 'startDistance', the distance (2-norm of the coordinates) from the via coordinates at which the blending starts; 'minDistance', the closest the blended trajectory comes to them; with a kinematicChain (Robot.GetKinematicChain()), also 'viaToolPosition', 'toolStartDistance' and 'toolMinDistance', the same for the position of the tool
- **input**:
  - `kinematicChain`: an exudyn.cUtilities.KinematicChain of the robot, for the distances of the tool; None: the coordinates only
  - `numberOfSamples`: the number of times in each blending at which the distances are evaluated
- **output**: a list of dicts
